comment: 3 and the sweeps. With a selection, Delete and Backspace did nothing and the history did not move (the 13-after-delete-and-backspace.png is the before). Here bare Backspace and bare Delete each clear only the selected area in one history step, a name field and a value slider keep their own Backspace, nothing selected clears the whole layer and says so, and the Krita profile gives Delete back to the background fill and keeps the clear on Backspace.

Every docker parked, then the Layers and Tool Options placed where an earlier layout had them, clear of the Colour Picker and the Minimap, because steps 04 and 05 aim at a row in one and a slider in the other.

The Layers docker's name field, open on Layer 1 with Sky typed into it. A click on the row first, through the root as a pen's would, so the docker's window holds the keyboard as it does under a painter's double click: the key step goes to whichever window holds it. Backspace takes the y off the name and leaves the selection's paint and the history where they were.
The pointer over the Tool Options docker's Flow slider. Backspace puts the slider back to the value it was built with and the layer keeps its paint, where before the router's gate the press did both.
Nothing selected. Backspace clears the whole layer and the corner says so.
The Krita profile, through the Keyboard Shortcuts page. Delete is the background fill there, as Krita ships it, and Backspace the clear alone.
Sara Default put back, so the painter's profile is what the next run starts on.

14 and the sweeps. Ctrl+Shift+C, Copy Merged in Krita and Photoshop, tinted the canvas and started a note (the 41-ctrl-shift-c-takes-a-note.png is the before). Here it starts nothing, and Ctrl+Alt+N starts the note and Escape leaves it. The log says SaNoteMode: on once, after Ctrl+Alt+N.
